articleSummary: 2.3 million cancers diagnosed in 2024 worldwide are attributable to infections, about one in eight cancers globally. The Lancet Oncology study by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) evaluated 12 infectious agents; five drive the majority: Helicobacter pylori (760,000 cases), human papillomavirus (HPV, 750,000), hepatitis B virus (HBV, 360,000), Epstein–Barr virus (EBV, 260,000), and hepatitis C virus (HCV, 160,000). East Asia accounts for 42% of infection-related cancers, with strong contributions from H. pylori and HBV; Sub-Saharan Africa contributes 28.5%, where HPV and the virus responsible for Kaposi’s sarcoma are among the main agents. Over 75% of these cancers occur in low- or middle-income countries. Prevention is pivotal: HPV and HBV vaccination, plus screening and treatment of infections; calls to develop vaccines against EBV and other oncogenic agents lacking preventive measures.

articleHeadline: Five-Year Study Reveals How Respiratory Pathogens Resurged After COVID-19
articleSummary: China-based five-year retrospective study of 9,674 patients with acute respiratory infection treated 2021–2025, from Hebei General Hospital and Hebei Medical University, shows suppression of pathogen circulation during strict NPIs, then a surge after relaxation, following China's December 2022 lifting of non-pharmaceutical interventions. Odds of detection rose in 2023–2025 vs 2021. The authors discuss immunity debt and frame findings as descriptive surveillance; no direct mechanism proven.

articleSummary: Two patients at Nghe An Friendship General Hospital in Vietnam were diagnosed with Whitmore's disease (melioidosis) from Burkholderia pseudomallei. She required mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, and continuous renal replacement therapy, was extubated after 12 days, and stabilized after three weeks of treatment. A male patient (born 1982) presented after four days of fever with rigors, cough, and dyspnea, developing septic shock, severe respiratory failure, AKI, and metabolic disturbances; blood cultures grew B. pseudomallei after 2 days. He was ventilated for 5 days and vasopressors were discontinued. Clinicians warn melioidosis can rapidly progress to pneumonia, bacteremia, and septic shock, especially during rainy seasons and floods; preventive measures include boots, gloves for mud/water, covering wounds, and prompt medical care for fever or respiratory symptoms.
